claim_text: §1's identity (U[f1]·W)·(W⁻¹·Z·W⁻ᵀ)·(U[f2]·W)ᵀ = U[f1]·Z·U[f2]ᵀ is correct but unconstrained; it says nothing about whether a non-trivial invertible W keeps U·W and transformed Z non-negative (clamp_(min=1e-7), ticket 74); §1's 'Established' status was never checked against whether this freedom is reachable by a real fitted solution.

Near-separability Tier 1 method: from NMF identifiability literature (Donoho & Stodden 2003; Arora et al. 2012; Huang/Sidiropoulos/Swami 2014), if every community has a near-pure entity in some facet that is strong evidence against reachable blending. Checked across all 6 configs × K∈{3,4}, live entities only (build_presence_masks), purity thresholds 0.5/0.7/0.85.

Known confound: evaluate_socio_semantic_reality's Part B (Doxa hoarding, MAX_MONOPOLY=0.85, chunk13v9.py:1160-1211) penalizes U_prob row-max >0.85 for 4 semantic target_facets only when structurally-propagated signal is spread; auth/affil/journ/art untouched by Part B; each purity witness's degree recorded to check against this confound.

Result table: at threshold 0.5, clean facets 56/56 (100%), confounded 46/48 (96%); at 0.7, 53/56 (95%) / 44/48 (92%); at 0.85, 49/56 (88%) / 41/48 (85%). Even at the strict 0.85 bar most (config,K,facet) cells have a near-pure witness for every community; art (most-connected facet) cleanly assigned with witness degree 60-80.

Correction: original text wrongly stated 0.85-bar failures were '7 of ~104 confounded cells; none in clean facets' naming 3 fringe_atom cells. Correct: 7/48 confounded-facet cells AND 7/56 clean-facet cells (14 total); the 'clean' bucket is actually 5 facets (includes parent_he), and 3 of the 7 clean-bucket failures are parent_he (C2/K3 0.522, C2/K4 0.824, C3/K4 0.650) — parent_he is outside Part B's target_facets (ticket 66, 'flagged, not decided'), so these are real unconfounded near-separability failures.
Remaining 4 clean-bucket failures are auth (C2/K4, C6/K4) and journ (C4/K4 non-converged, C6/K3).

fringe_atom is the recurring confounded-bucket failure in 4 cells, not 3: C1/K4, C3/K4, C4/K4, and C5/K4 (previously omitted). Of the 7 confounded-bucket failures, 4 (not 3) are not fully explained by the Part B/low-degree confound: C1/K4/fringe_atom, C3/K4/cousin_he, C3/K4/fringe_atom, C4/K4/fringe_atom (non-converged, flagged per SESSION_PROTOCOL rule 4).

Near-separability is sufficient, not necessary — its presence is strong practical evidence against reachable blending, but absence in some cells doesn't prove blending is reachable there; a decisive answer requires Tier 2's direct feasibility search for a non-trivial orthogonal W.

Tier 2 method: for each fitted (U_final,Z_final) searched for the largest Givens rotation W(θ) mixing exactly two communities, applied to U_final and Z_final for every active facet/relation simultaneously, before any monitored entry goes negative; excludes ticket 79's rescaling freedom; sweeping all K(K-1)/2 pairwise generators is a complete local check of the tangent space. Coarse scan 0.5°-90° then bisection; same 6 configs × K∈{3,4} grid.

Methodological history: first run used absolute tolerance (reject entry below -1e-4) and returned 0.00° margin for all 54 pairs uniformly, flagged as too clean to trust; diagnosed as floor-clamped entries triggering at vanishing angle; fix applied at the time: monitor only entries ≥1% of column/relation max (MEANINGFUL_FRAC=0.01), producing the originally-reported 0.5°-3.4° margin result.

A later audit pass found MEANINGFUL_FRAC flawed: on C6/K4's auth facet the column-relative 1% mask monitored only 18.3% of entries; averaged across the grid 78-84% of U was excluded per cell; excluded entries are disproportionately the near-zero entries in a witness's other communities — exactly what a blending rotation pushes negative first. Concrete case: a witness row had U_prob=0.071 (U_norm=0.00192, a real non-floor value) excluded solely for sitting below 1% of that column's max.

Corrected re-run replaced the column-relative mask with an absolute one calibrated against the model's clamp floor: literal floor-clamped entries cluster at ≈1.5e-7 (35% of entries), a further 44% sit in [1e-6,1e-4); set FLOOR_EXCLUDE=1e-6 and tightened TOL from 1e-4 to 1e-8 accordingly.

Result: 53 of 54 pairs pinned below 0.05°, most exactly 0.000° in at least one direction (max margin anywhere: 0.57°, C2/K4 pair (1,3)). The 0.5°-3.4° figures previously in this document are superseded and should not be used — they measured feasibility of a masked subproblem, not the real system.

Numerical-precision check: only 3/54 pairs pinned at exactly 0.000° in both directions; 33/54 have neither direction at exact zero; 18/54 show real directional asymmetry between +margin and -margin — pattern is structured, consistent with genuine constraint-binding, not a uniform floating-point collapse.

Scope: this is a local (first-order/infinitesimal) feasibility bound around the fitted solution, not proof no distant rotation loops back to a different feasible point. Within that scope, the corrected finding strengthens §18's conclusion: genuine local blending freedom is essentially absent almost everywhere tested, and now agrees with (rather than contradicts) the original pre-MEANINGFUL_FRAC 0.00°-everywhere run.

Motivation for the distant-rotation extension: any rotation, local or distant, that stays feasible has exactly the same reconstruction loss as the original fit (per §1's exact identity) — unlike a different-seed/different-basin disagreement (§1's Run 2 vs Run 4: recon_loss 0.7593 vs 0.7591, opposite anchor-coherence structure), which loss can distinguish. A distant feasible rotation would be invisible to loss-based selection by construction.
ground_truth_hint: FINDINGS.md §1 Run 2 vs Run 4 recon_loss figures

claim_text: Swept ±90° at fine resolution for all 54 pairs; first pass used 1° step and found zero islands, but local margins are sub-degree so a 1° grid could miss a comparable-width island; re-ran at 0.05° (36× finer), same result, and recovered cage widths independently match bisection margins (e.g. C5/K4 pair (0,1): -0.65°/+0.75° vs -1.03°/+0.55°). Result: 0 of 54 pairs have more than one feasible region at either resolution.

Scope limits on the distant-rotation extension: only single-pair rotations swept, one at a time — a joint rotation moving several community pairs simultaneously was not searched; 0.05° resolution is still a discrete grid that could in principle miss a narrower island.
ground_truth_hint: n/a — stated scope limitation, joint multi-pair rotation search not built

claim_text: Caveat raised on audit pass: this extension originally inherited the flawed MEANINGFUL_FRAC mask, and its cross-check against bisection margins had only been validated against the now-superseded 0.5°-3.4° numbers; predicted the '0 islands' verdict would plausibly survive the fix since a stricter check can only shrink or preserve a feasible region.

Re-run under the identical corrected mask (FLOOR_EXCLUDE=1e-6, TOL=1e-8), 0.05°-step sweep across ±90°, all 54 pairs, all 12 cells: 0 of 54 pairs show more than one feasible region. Run boundaries tighter than the superseded run — mostly within hundredths to ~0.15° of zero, several pinned at machine precision on both sides.

Diagnostic scripts: rotation_island_search.py (superseded methodology, kept for historical record) and rotation_island_search_v2.py (corrected, absolute-floor-mask version, authoritative). Results in rotation_island_search.json (superseded) and rotation_island_search_v2.json (authoritative).

Practical implication (Tier1+Tier2 combined): at production settings, Layer 1b's blending freedom is essentially absent locally, not merely narrow — a cleaner, stronger conclusion than the original 'narrow but real' framing. Model outputs (U_prob, Z-based coupling) for one specific reported fit are more trustworthy against this failure mode than previously stated; cross-fit/cross-seed comparisons still require relabeling correction (§14/§16/§17) — a different problem (§19), not addressed by this section.

fringe_atom (Tier1's recurring failure, confirmed 4 cells not 3) is worth extra scrutiny before relying on its community assignments across fits, and the previously-overlooked parent_he clean-bucket failures deserve the same caution. Toy-corpus-calibrated — re-derive at 22k-article scale before trusting; a denser corpus could tighten or loosen these margins either way.

claim_text: Diagnostic scripts: near_separability_check.py, rotation_feasibility_search.py (superseded, kept for historical record), rotation_feasibility_search_v2.py (corrected, authoritative for Tier2 margins). Results in near_separability_check.json, rotation_feasibility_search.json (superseded), rotation_feasibility_search_v2.json (authoritative).

Re-derivation on post-08-27-fix data (tickets 86/87 Stage 0e): all three scripts re-run unmodified; table: Tier1 0.85-bar failures clean facets 7/56→3/56, confounded 7/48→7/48, total 14→10; Tier2 local pairs pinned below 0.05°: 53/54→53/54; Tier2 max single-directional margin: 0.57° (C2/K4 pair(1,3)) → 0.325° (C5/K3 pair(0,2)); Tier2 distant pairs with second feasible region: 0/54→0/54.

Every number moved the same direction as, or held exactly at, the standing conclusion: Tier1 purity-witness coverage improved (14→10 failures), Tier2's worst-case local rotation margin shrank (0.57°→0.325°), Tier2's distant search still finds zero disconnected feasible regions. This is a confirmation, not a correction, of §18's conclusion.

Non-content change: which single grid cell fails to converge shifted — old flagged C4/K4 (Tier1) / C3/K4+C4/K4 (Tier2 local); new flags only C3/K4 in both. Consistent with this project's already-documented single-seed fit sensitivity (ticket 85), not a new instability; retained in results per SESSION_PROTOCOL §C.4.
Scripts unchanged for the post-08-27-fix re-derivation (re-run as-is, no code modified). Results in near_separability_check.json, rotation_feasibility_search_v2.json, rotation_island_search_v2.json.

A community's domain-skew identity is not reproducible across independently-trained seeds — confirmed with the pipeline's own §S5 alignment, not just a weaker proxy. Distinct from §18 (this is problem 1a, relabeling across independently-trained fits, not 1b, local rotation freedom within one fit) — the two should not be conflated.

Question: does a community's apparent domain character survive across independent re-fits of the same (config,K), or does it reshuffle? Answering requires aligning communities across seeds first — community index is only meaningful within one fit (§14).

First pass: measured with a single-facet (art-only) Hungarian match on column-similarity, the simplest alignment available, not the pipeline's own method. Result: ~45% (19/42) of (config,K,community) triples had a sign-consistent domain-skew reading across 5 seeds (1000/2000/3000/4000/5000), C1-C6 × K∈{3,4}. Never written up formally.

Corrected measurement re-ran the identical design aligning seeds with run_dual_track_stability_analysis's actual method (Module 4 §5): all facets stacked, two independent tracks (Track A JSD, Track B magnitude-weighted cosine), each via linear_sum_assignment. Implemented as faithful reuse: diagnostic_blocks.s5_dual_track_alignment calls row_normalize/col_normalize/row_wise_cosine_similarity directly off the loaded chunk13v9.py module.
ground_truth_hint: chunk13v9.py: grep run_dual_track_stability_analysis; diagnostic_blocks.py: grep s5_dual_track_alignment

claim_text: The concern (that weak alignment understated stability) was refuted in the opposite direction from how it was raised — stability was slightly lower under the stronger method: art-only 45% (19/42), §S5 Track A (JSD) 38% (16/42), §S5 Track B (weighted cosine) 40% (17/42).

New finding, only visible with two independent tracks: Track A and Track B agree with each other on only 42/48 (88%) of seed pairs — in 12% of pairs the pipeline's own best method disagrees with itself about which community is which. C3/K4 is the extreme case (1/4 pairs agree; one of its 5 seeds did not converge).

Per-config (Track A), same qualitative pattern as informal first pass, not improved by the stronger method: C1 0/7 (0%), C2 6/7 (86%), C3/C4/C5 ~29% each, C6 4/7 (57%). Denser, more anchor-supported topologies (C2, C6) remain more stable than single-anchor C1 — consistent with §4.15's independent finding about C1's anchor weakness.

Practical implication: the hypothesis that a weak alignment method caused apparently low reproducibility is refuted, not confirmed — the weaker method appears to have overstated stability. A community's domain-skew identity is not a robust, reproducible property across independent re-fits, even measured by the pipeline's own best available tool.

Calibration against chance: 'stable' requires all 5 seeds to share the reference seed's sign; under a fair-coin null the probability of the 4 non-reference seeds all matching by chance is (1/2)^4=6.25%. The observed 38-40% is roughly 6× the chance rate — real, detectable consistency, just far short of reliable ('far above chance, far below reliable').

This sharpens the concern about interpreting domain-skew labels as substantive across anything other than one specific reported fit, consistent with the caveat throughout this document that cross-fit/cross-seed comparisons require relabeling correction (§14/§16/§17). Toy-corpus-calibrated — re-derive at 22k-article scale; a denser corpus could change this either way.

Diagnostic script domain_skew_s5_alignment_reproducibility.py reuses the new diagnostic_blocks.s5_dual_track_alignment (BLOCKS_VERSION 1.8.0); results in domain_skew_s5_alignment_reproducibility.json.

The 38-40% figure is a binary sign-flip on a derived, sometimes near-zero quantity, overstating severity. Extracted the continuous similarity scores (mean_js_sim, weighted_cos_sim per facet) via new diagnostic_blocks.s5_dual_track_consensus (BLOCKS_VERSION 1.9.0). Mean global consensus across all 12 cells: 0.667 (Track A) / 0.670 (Track B), range 0.52-0.78 — a real, moderate number, not near-zero or near-perfect.

The same configs rank the same way under both measures: C1 and C3/K4 (non-converged) weakest under both sign-flip and continuous measure; C2/C6 (dual-anchor) strongest under both. The two tests disagree only on how alarming the headline number is, not on which configs are more reproducible.

New signal cross-validating §18: per-facet, art and anchor-adjacent semantic facets (parent_he, core_child_he, cousin_he) consistently score high (0.8-0.99, especially Track B); fringe_atom is consistently the weakest/most erratic facet (often below 0.5), core_atom and affil also often weak. fringe_atom is the same facet §18's Tier 1 independently flagged as its recurring failure — two unrelated methods converging on the same weak point.

Practical implication: a defensible cross-seed robustness statement is '~0.65-0.70 average alignment consensus, weaker for C1 and fringe_atom, stronger for C2/C6 and anchor-adjacent facets' — moderate and real, not near-random, but not a clean bill of health either. Toy-corpus-calibrated.
Diagnostic script domain_skew_s5_continuous_consensus.py; results in domain_skew_s5_continuous_consensus.json.

Raised in discussion: a 'stable core / variable periphery' story to explain the fringe_atom/C1 weakness pattern. Flagged as a mere association until tested against alternatives (pure facet effect, pure config effect, unstructured noise) — two analyses (Part A re-decomposition, Part B new per-entity test) run to separate them.

Part A: facet and config effects are both real and additive, not competing. fringe_atom is weak in every config including the strongest (C6: -0.159 below that config's own mean; C2: -0.170). C1 is weak across 7 of 9 facets, including ones strong elsewhere (core_child_he: -0.166 below that facet's own mean). A simple additive model (grand mean + facet effect + config effect) explains 78% of the total variance; residual 22% is interaction or noise.

Part B per-entity correlation table (within config×facet cells): Degree vs Track A mean ρ=+0.011 (23/104 sig pos, 14/104 sig neg); Degree vs Track B mean ρ=+0.053 (27/104, 13/104); U_prob purity vs Track A mean ρ=+0.177 (54/104 sig pos, 24/104 sig neg); purity vs Track B mean ρ=+0.073 (39/104, 31/104). Raw connectivity does not predict individual stability (near-zero mean correlation); confidence of assignment shows a real but partial, inconsistent signal.

Caveat: purity and Track A's similarity measure are both derived from the same row-normalized distribution, so part of the purity/Track-A correlation may reflect mathematical kinship rather than fully independent confirmation — the weaker Track B result (close to a coin flip) is probably the more trustworthy read of the effect's real strength.

Revised conclusion: the 'central core, drifting periphery' story is not supported. What drives cross-seed reproducibility is mostly which facet and which config (additive, 78% of variance), not entity centrality. A confidence-based partial effect exists but is inconsistent, not a reliable law; the unexplained residual is consistent with genuine unstructured noise, though not directly provable.

Scope not tested: 'centrality' here meant only raw degree and U_prob row-max ('purity'); no graph-theoretic centrality (eigenvector/PageRank/Katz) was tried, and no hypergraph-specific centrality measure was tried for the hyperedge facets. Not a claim these are the right measures — a future revisit should try at least eigenvector/Katz centrality before concluding the core/periphery story is fully closed.
ground_truth_hint: n/a — eigenvector/Katz centrality analysis not built

claim_text: Diagnostic script core_periphery_stability_test.py; results in core_periphery_stability_test.json.

Problem 2 title/status: is collapse_pen (Z_scaled-based) gameable in a way that distorts model selection? T1 almost never engages; T2 engages regularly and the exploit pattern was directly observed. Status: partially established, toy corpus only; collapse_pen's near-total inertness is a T1-slice/K=4-specific finding, not a general property of the model.
ground_truth_hint: note: this claim is later revised by the CORRECTION subsection at FINDINGS.md line ~2241

claim_text: The concern precisely: collapse_pen is the only quantity that is (a) derived from Z_scaled and (b) read by Optuna every trial, feeding sociological_penalty (§4.17/§4.20; ticket 81). Worry: Z_scaled can be reshaped by the optimizer without genuine reconstruction change (the same scale-invariance slack §4.2 already closed once for z_offdiag_loss), showing up as a collapse_pen improvement not corresponding to real de-concentration of entities.

Method: two new diagnostic_blocks.py helpers (BLOCKS_VERSION 1.9.0→1.10.0): collapse_mass_share (not a reimplementation — calls production's own _relation_community_share; self-checked, matches evaluate_dimensional_collapse's collapse_score to 0.00e+00) and membership_share_all_facets (pools live-entity mean U_prob rows across all 9 facets with equal weight, never touches Z_scaled).
Test 2 first pass, C1-C6 × K∈{2,4}, production settings: solution-level Pearson r=0.956, Spearman r=0.944; 2/12 cells showed the exploit pattern (mass_max≤0.60 while mem_max>0.60: C2/K2, C6/K2).

Correction: K=2 was flagged as too low-information to trust (with 2 communities both share vectors are mechanically pinned near 0.5). Re-run on K∈{3,4}: solution-level Pearson r=0.506 (p=0.093, not significant), Spearman r=0.748 (p=0.0051); community-level Pearson r=0.420 (p=0.0056), down from 0.872. The K=2-inclusive correlation was substantially inflated by low degrees of freedom. 0/12 cells showed the exploit pattern at K∈{3,4}.

Test 1: hand-picked lambda_z_offdiag sweep (0.0→2.0, 40× production), C1-C6 × K∈{3,4}, 48 fits. collapse_pen fired in only 1/48 fits (0.0028, C1/K=4 at lz=2.0). Raising lambda_z_offdiag mostly increased mass_max (10/12 cells) — opposite of what a 'cheap collapse_pen improvement' exploit would need. Correlation between mass_max delta and mem_max delta was weak, not significant: Pearson r=0.478 (p=0.116), Spearman r=0.357 (p=0.255). One cell (C3/K=4) showed the exploit shape in its delta but collapse_pen was 0.0 both before and after.

Test 3 (a U_scales-shrinking signature check) was deliberately not run: collapse_pen is built on Z_scaled specifically because §4.2 already closes the U_scales-inflation/Z_pos-shrinkage loophole by construction, and Tests 1-2 show little live pressure for that mechanism to matter in practice. Skipped by agreement, low expected value.

Test 4 intro: a real Optuna study letting NSGAIISampler search lambda_z_offdiag ~ log-uniform[1e-4,1.0] (the real search space, lambda_l1=0 fixed per ticket 78) — testing whether the actual search process finds and exploits the proxy, not just whether it's hackable in principle (citing Skalse, Howe, Krasheninnikov & Krueger NeurIPS 2022; van Laarhoven 2017 — citations from memory, flagged for verification before formal use).

Design: faithfully mirrors create_optuna_objective's real sequence (run_inner_solver → evaluate_complete_solution, same lambda handling, same NSGAIISampler(seed=MASTER_SEED)) called directly against the loaded module, but written as a parallel inline copy so U_final/Z_final could be captured per trial. Module 4 was not exercised at all — in-memory Optuna storage, n_trials=20 per cell (not production's SCOUT_TRIALS=100). Grid: C1-C6 × K∈{3,4}, T1 slice, 240 trials, 23.8 min wall time.

Limit caught on a later audit pass: NSGAIISampler's default population_size is 50 (verified against installed optuna==4.9.0); at n_trials=20 per cell the run never completes even one generation, so NSGA-II's selection/crossover machinery never activates — every trial is drawn from the sampler's initial random-population phase. Shows the proxy is not hackable under pure random search, but does not show whether NSGA-II's own optimization pressure would seek out and exploit a gap.
ground_truth_hint: python -c "import optuna; print(optuna.samplers.NSGAIISampler().__init__.__defaults__)" or check installed optuna==4.9.0 default population_size

claim_text: Because a fresh NSGAIISampler(seed=MASTER_SEED) is constructed once per cell, all 12 cells draw the identical 20 lambda_z_offdiag values (confirmed directly from stored records) — the 240 trials are 20 distinct lambda draws × 12 cells, not 240 independent samples; reported p-values should be read as optimistic, though point estimates are unaffected. This pairing is useful for the T1-vs-T2 comparison specifically.
ground_truth_hint: diagnostic_results/collapse_pen_optuna_study.json — verify identical lambda draws across cells

claim_text: collapse_pen fired zero times across all 240 real search trials on T1 — never once, across the full lambda range Optuna is permitted to explore. Exploit pattern also never occurred (0/240). Pooled correlation across 220 converged trials: Pearson r=0.220 (p=0.0010), Spearman r=0.201 (p=0.0027) — statistically significant but numerically weak.

Conclusion for Problem 2, T1 only: the original worry has nowhere to operate in this regime, because collapse_pen essentially never becomes an active constraint for the real search to exploit. Flagged at the time as scoped, not a general exoneration — correctly so, per the T2 replication.

T2 replication: identical design (collapse_pen_optuna_study_t2.py), run against the T2 slice (36 articles, 4,158 total non-zero relational entries) instead of T1 (25/3,323), to check whether T1's small article count was itself a factor. 240 trials, 24.2 min.

collapse_pen fired 25/240 times on T2 — all at K=3, zero at K=4 in any config, concentrated in C2/K3 (12 fires) and C6/K3 (10 fires), both clustered at low lambda_z_offdiag (mostly ≤0.0031, near the search floor); C3/K3 (1) and C5/K3 (2) show a different mid-range-lambda pattern. T1's 'essentially never fires' conclusion does not generalise past K=4 or past the T1 slice.

The exploit pattern occurred 4/240 trials, all in C5/K3: at lambda_z_offdiag 0.6351/0.2915/0.7579/0.2137, mass_max was 0.484/0.496/0.480/0.580 while mem_max was 0.630/0.613/0.634/0.604, and collapse_pen read 0.0000 in all four (all converged). All four sit at the high end of lambda_z_offdiag (0.21-0.76), opposite the end where collapse_pen actually fires in this same config.

This is directly consistent with the mechanism §2 already confirmed once for z_offdiag_loss: raising lambda_z_offdiag can move Z_scaled's readout toward 'looks balanced' via the community-resizing route rather than genuine de-concentration.

Stronger than '4/240' alone suggests, checked on a later audit pass: each cell drew 20 trials from only 19 distinct lambda_z_offdiag values (one repeat); the 4 flagged trials in C5/K3 are exactly the 4 highest of those 19 draws — 4 of 4 high-lambda draws show the pattern, not 4 scattered flukes. Only 4 of 19 draws exceed lambda_z_offdiag=0.2, so the high-lambda regime is thinly sampled.

Naming caveat: 'exploit pattern' implies mass_max and mem_max are two readings of the same underlying quantity, one gamed and one honest — they are not (mass_max is relation-mass-weighted permutation-corrected share; mem_max is unweighted equal-per-facet entity fraction). No tested baseline exists for how much they'd diverge with no lambda-driven distortion at all; 'divergence pattern, concentrated at high lambda' is a more precise description than 'exploit pattern'.

Pooled correlation on T2 (210 converged trials): Pearson r=0.331 (p<0.0001), Spearman r=0.525 (p<0.0001) — both higher than T1's (Pearson 0.220, Spearman 0.201), so mass_max/mem_max track each other somewhat better on T2 even though collapse_pen engages more.

Revised conclusion: collapse_pen's inertness was T1/K=4-specific, not a property of the model. At K=3 on the larger T2 slice it is a real, occasionally-active constraint, and the specific gaming pattern Problem 2 was worried about has now been observed directly, concentrated at high lambda_z_offdiag in C5.
ground_truth_hint: diagnostic_results/collapse_pen_optuna_study_t2.json — note this claim is itself withdrawn later, tickets 86/87 Stage 0e

claim_text: This raises the priority of Problem 2 relative to the T1-only round — not a closed question. The next natural step, a K=3-focused, C5-focused deeper sweep to see how far the exploit pattern extends, had not yet been run at time of writing.

claim_text: CORRECTION (tickets 86/87 Stage 0e): on post-08-27-fix data the observed exploit pattern does not reproduce — the directly-observed gaming evidence reported above is withdrawn.

collapse_pen_optuna_study_v2.py (100 trials/cell, 24 cells, 2,400 trials) re-run on corrected data: T2 trials where collapse_pen fired: 118/1,200 (pre-fix) → 6/1,200 (post-fix); T2 exploit-pattern trials: 18→0; T1 fired/exploit 0/0 both; T1 pooled corr Pearson/Spearman 0.381/0.375→0.564/0.576; T2 pooled corr 0.360/0.547→0.435/0.439. All 18 pre-fix exploit instances sat in T2/C5/K3 and are now absent; per-cell firing dropped C2/K3 53→0, C3/K3 3→0, C5/K3 24→0, C6/K3 38→6; all four cells converged 100/100 in both runs, so not a convergence artifact.

Mechanism visible in distributions: pre-fix T2 had 11.0% of converged trials with mass_max above the 0.60 threshold (reaching 0.772); post-fix only 0.5% do (reaching 0.655). mem_max above 0.60 fell from 1.7% (max 0.640) to none (max 0.521). The extreme concentration that triggered both the penalty and the exploit pattern is no longer produced.

Most plausible cause (a hypothesis, could not be verified directly): before the journal-resolution fix, repositories (arXiv etc.) were treated as journals, so a single journ node connected many articles, pulling articles into one community and inflating mass_max; S_Art_Journ fell from 35 to 13 ties in T2 when those were removed. Could not be confirmed because the pre-fix pickles were regenerated in place and no longer exist.
ground_truth_hint: pre-fix matrices no longer exist to verify; cross-ref CLAUDE.md §4.23, FINDINGS §11

claim_text: What survives: the structural argument that collapse_pen reads one Z_scaled-derived scalar carrying ticket-79 gauge freedom, Test 1's exploitability sweep, and §22's evidence a Z_scaled-based domain-balance candidate was gamed 30-40x. What does not survive: the claim that the exploit pattern has been observed occurring in a realistic Optuna search — on corrected data across 2,400 trials it occurs zero times. Problem 2 returns to 'a structurally real risk not observed in practice on this corpus.'

Convergence in this run: T1 1,126/1,200 and T2 1,130/1,200 trials converged; weakest cells T1/C4/K=4 (45/100) and T2/C5/K=4 (33/100). Run note: study executed in two parts (18 cells initial, 6 cells resumed after wall-clock limit) differing in PYTHONHASHSEED (open ticket 85); cells are independent studies so per-slice pooled statistics are unaffected, split recorded in resume_events.

T1 (Test 4) convergence at K=4: C4/K4 9/20 (45%), C2/K4 14/20 (70%), C3/K4 17/20 (85%), C1/K4/C5/K4/C6/K4 all 20/20. C2/K4's 6 failures and 10 of C4/K4's 11 failures cluster at lambda_z_offdiag≤0.0031; the identical near-zero lambda draws converged without issue on C1/C5/C6/K4 — so this is C2/C4-specific, not a general low-lambda effect.

T2 replication convergence at K=4 markedly worse: C4/K4 only 3/20 (15%), C3/K4 only 7/20 (35%); C1/C2/C5/C6/K4 all recovered to 20/20. Every T2 K=4 failure hit exactly the 2000-epoch ceiling, and failure lambdas spread across nearly the entire search range, unlike T1's floor-clustering; T2's average epoch counts were much higher (572-1975) — a different mechanism from T1's.

Combined verdict: C4/K4 is the weakest cell on both slices (45%→15% converged, T1→T2), the single most consistent piece of negative evidence against any config in this document. C3/K4 is weak specifically at T2 scale, not T1. These are unrelated to C1's separately-known single-anchor weakness (§4.15) — three different configs, three different mechanisms.

Follow-up question: does Z_scaled's full diagonal/off-diagonal pattern (not just collapse_pen's one scalar) track independent structure? Answer: yes, moderately, and the decline under lambda_z_offdiag pressure is confirmed real, not noise. collapse_pen reads only max_share; this says nothing about whether the raw diagonal/off-diagonal values §1 and this document's community-coupling interpretation depend on can be reshaped by the same training-dynamics-driven slack.

Method: an independent reading data_reading[k1,k2] = U_prob_f1[:,k1]ᵀ @ X_r @ U_prob_f2[:,k2], measuring how much of a relation's real raw edges connect entities plausibly in k1/k2, never touching Z, compared against Z_scaled's own full K×K reading, both normalised to sum to 1 (diagonal and off-diagonal).

A methodological correction happened mid-investigation: the first version read Z_scaled as raw |Z[k1,k2]| shares with no Hungarian permutation correction, flagged as possibly flawed since §14 documents a relation's raw diagonal can be legitimately scrambled. The 'fix' extended _hungarian_relabel_relation to the full K×K matrix (diagnostic_blocks.relation_share_matrix, self-checked bit-for-bit against production's diagonal, 0.00e+00 diff).
Applying the Hungarian-correction 'fix' made every correlation weaker, not stronger: pooled Spearman 0.663→0.599; diagonal 0.660→0.562; off-diagonal 0.422→0.343.

Working through why revealed the fix was based on a wrong diagnosis: Z[k1,k2] is already indexed by U_prob_f1's own column k1 and U_prob_f2's own column k2 by construction — there is no representational ambiguity to correct for against data_share's native indexing. _hungarian_relabel_relation corrects a different problem (community index offset across facets, relevant to collapse_pen's aggregate accounting); applying it here breaks alignment rather than fixing it. Conclusion: the original raw (uncorrected) method was the methodologically appropriate one — reverted to it as primary.

Primary result (raw method, confirmed across two independent runs on the same 48 cached T1 fits): pooled Pearson r=0.733, Spearman r=0.660 (n=4,588) — meaningfully stronger than the max_share-only comparison. Diagonal (n=1,288): Pearson r=0.613, Spearman r=0.656. Off-diagonal (n=3,300): Pearson r=0.630, Spearman r=0.416.

Spearman shows off-diagonal terms tracking the independent reading noticeably worse than diagonal terms — within-community coupling readings from Z_scaled are more trustworthy than between-community coupling readings; an explicit caveat is warranted wherever the article leans on Z's off-diagonal to claim a between-community relationship.
Under increasing lambda_z_offdiag pressure (0.0→2.0), correspondence declines mildly but consistently: Spearman falls 0.693→0.677→0.638→0.595 (Pearson: 0.765→0.737→0.747→0.723) — a decline of 0.098.

Calibration check: re-ran the correlation across 5 independent seeds at fixed production lambda_z_offdiag=0.05, same C1-C6×K∈{3,4} grid (60 fits, 1 non-converged excluded: C3/K4/seed=2000). Seed-to-seed Spearman spread at fixed lambda: 0.035 (range [0.682, 0.717]). The lambda-driven decline (0.098) is 2.8× the seed-to-seed baseline spread — the erosion under lambda_z_offdiag pressure is a real, lambda-driven effect, not ordinary seed variability.

Net effect: Z_scaled's full diagonal/off-diagonal pattern is meaningfully grounded in real structure overall, but off-diagonal values specifically are the weaker link and their correspondence erodes under lambda_z_offdiag pressure by a margin confirmed to exceed noise. Distinct from §18 (which tested static rotational freedom within one fit, found narrow) — related but not the same question. This test used T1 only; not yet replicated on T2.

claim_text: Method (mass_mem_argmax_decomposition.py): a controlled sweep, not an Optuna search — C1/C2/C3 × K∈{3,4}, T1 only, lambda_z_offdiag fixed at 7 log-spaced values from 1e-4 to 1.0 (cached single fits, production settings). Records both argmax communities, whether they match ('identity match'), and how many individual sources feeding each aggregate pick the same community as the aggregate ('internal agreement').

Result 1 identity match rate table (argmax(mass)==argmax(mem)): C1/K3 7/7 both; C1/K4 3/7→4/7; C2/K3 4/7→7/7; C2/K4 2/5→4/7; C3/K3 1/7→3/7; C3/K4 3/5→1/6; all cells 20/38 (53%)→26/41 (63%). Result 2, internal agreement at production lambda_z_offdiag=0.05: mass_share's aggregate winner is the first choice of only 1-4 of 8 relations in every cell; mem_share's winner is usually a majority pick (4-7 of 9 facets post-fix). Worked example C3/K4 post-fix λ=0.05 (a mismatch case): mass_share names community 1, mem_share names community 3; community 0 is the plurality individual choice (4 of 8 relations) yet the average names community 1 because M_Cousin_Child places 0.639 of its mass on community 1 while community 0's four supporters place only ~0.31-0.42 each; 7 of 9 facets individually pick community 3 for mem_share.

What this establishes vs. doesn't: it establishes a precondition (collapse_pen reacts to whichever community currently holds the largest mass share, which could differ from the community holding the largest membership share), not a proven failure in any particular fit — the script doesn't record near-tie margins or seed-to-seed argmax variance. It qualifies, but does not change, §20's conclusions about gameability.

claim_text: D2's entity-weighted spread inflation, made exact: §13's update measured dev_k's spread growing under entity weighting (mean dev_k ≈0.08 equal-weighted → ≈0.13 entity-weighted), flagged as possibly mechanical. Derived exactly via soc_k=Σ_f w_f·p_f[k] model: idiosyncratic-noise contribution to Var(soc_k) is σ_e²·Σ_f w_f² (Herfindahl concentration index; 1/Σw_f² is Kish's effective sample size), minimized by equal weights.

Table: equal Σw² (n_eff) vs entity Σw² (n_eff) for social/semantic T1/T2, predicted SD ratio √(entity/equal): Social T1 0.250(4.0)→0.588(1.70), ratio 1.53×; Social T2 0.250(4.0)→0.577(1.73), 1.52×; Semantic T1 0.200(5.0)→0.238(4.21), 1.09×; Semantic T2 0.200(5.0)→0.237(4.23), 1.09×. Social collapses from an effective 4 facets to ~1.7 (auth's ~75% share); semantic barely moves (no facet exceeds ~32%).

Checked directly against actual sd(r_k): T1 equal 0.0967, entity 0.1519, observed ratio 1.571×, predicted ratio 1.533×; T2 equal 0.0977, entity 0.1417, observed ratio 1.450×, predicted ratio 1.519×. A parameter-free prediction from facet headcounts alone lands within 2-5% of the observed spread increase.

The mean/median shift toward semantic (mean(r_k) dropping from ≈0.494 to ≈0.465 under entity weighting, both slices, flagged in §13 as unexplained) is the same mechanism, not a second mystery. The hypothesis that auth is less decisively assigned than the small social facets was tested and refuted: auth's median row-max (0.999) is higher than journ's (0.934) or affil's (0.920), not lower.

Σ_k soc_k = 1 is an algebraic invariant for any weighting scheme, so mean_k(soc_k)=1/K identically under equal and entity weighting — confirmed: mean(soc_k)=0.2857(T1)/0.2941(T2) under both weightings, while var(soc_k) roughly doubles (0.0140→0.0336 T1, 2.39×; 0.0158→0.0408 T2, 2.58×) and 14.3%(T1)/5.9%(T2) of communities are pushed under soc_k=0.10 under entity weighting only (vs 0% equal).

r_k = soc_k/(soc_k+sem_k) is concave and increasing in soc_k for fixed sem_k; a variable with the same mean but higher variance passed through a concave function has a lower expected output, so entity weighting's Herfindahl-driven spread mechanically lowers mean(r_k) with no separate cause needed — the earlier 'unexplained, needs its own investigation' framing is withdrawn as the same mechanism as the spread increase.

The spread/mean analysis compares two weighting schemes against each other; it says nothing about how reliable a single fit's r_k reading is in absolute terms — the question needed to set TOL so it exceeds genuine noise rather than firing on communities that are not actually imbalanced, just unluckily seeded.

Method (domain_balance_seed_noise.py): for each (config,K,slice) cell, refit at 5 seeds (MASTER_SEED + 4 offsets), same data/hyperparameters (lambda_l1=0, lambda_z_offdiag=0.05), only RNG differs. Each non-reference seed is realigned onto the reference seed's labeling via s5_dual_track_alignment's Track A (JSD/probability-space Hungarian assignment) — faithful reuse of production's own §S5 stability-analysis alignment code. r_k (entity-weighted, u_prob space) recomputed under each seed's aligned labeling; across-seed SD per community is the noise floor. Smoke-tested: C1 (single-anchor) showed much larger seed-to-seed swings than C6 (dual-anchor) in a 2-seed pilot, confirming the alignment step is doing real work.

Full grid (C1-C6×K∈{3,4}×T1/T2, 5 seeds each; 76 usable community-cells, 2 skipped for reference-seed non-convergence: T2/C3/K4, T2/C4/K4): noise SD(r_k) mean 0.134, median 0.144, p90 0.192, max 0.229. Paired against each community's own dev_k: only 46% exceed own noise SD, 21% exceed 1.5×, 13% exceed 2×. Strongest genuine cases T1/C1/K4 comm1 (dev_k=0.108, noiseSD=0.024, ratio 4.5×) and T2/C2/K4 comm2 (dev_k=0.322, noiseSD=0.141, ratio 2.3×); weakest T1/C3/K3 comm2 (dev_k=0.009, noiseSD=0.140, ratio 0.06).

Per-configuration noise breakdown: C1 mean0.114/median0.137/max0.193; C2 0.135/0.135/0.193; C3 0.105/0.113/0.159; C4 0.156/0.163/0.178; C5 0.151/0.164/0.229; C6 0.144/0.148/0.216. No config outlier severe enough to exclude. C1 (documented weakest overall, §4.15) is the second-lowest noise config here, not the highest; dual-anchor configs (C2/C5/C6) are if anything slightly noisier than single-anchor (C1/C3/C4) — opposite of what §4.15's weakness would predict.

Decision: TOL=0.15 for the toy corpus (D3, closes the open item in §4.18/ticket 82), sitting just above the overall noise median. Caveat: C4/C5 T1 medians run 0.16-0.17, own local noise floor at/slightly above 0.15, some false-positive risk concentrated there. Explicitly a toy-corpus value, flagged for re-estimation on the 22k-article corpus, matching the pattern used for lambda_l1's bounds (ticket 77).

Re-derivation subsection: the measurement above used with-repository data (regenerated 2026-08-25/26, before the journal-resolution fix). Both domain_balance_seed_noise.py and domain_balance_measurement.py re-run unmodified on post-fix pickles, re-paired community-by-community on the same 24-cell grid, now fully converged — 84/84 community-cells usable vs 76/84 before (T2/C3/K4 and T2/C4/K4 now fit cleanly).

Table old(with-repository) vs new(post-fix): noise SD(r_k) mean/median/p90/max 0.134/0.144/0.192/0.229 → 0.119/0.120/0.172/0.234; dev_k median 0.112→0.093; %communities dev_k>1×noiseSD 46%→36%(30/84); >1.5× 21%→15.5%(13/84); >2× 13%→4.8%(4/84); >TOL(0.15) outright — 19%(16/84). Both noise floor and signal shrank comparably; the fraction whose apparent imbalance survives its own seed-noise floor dropped at every multiple tested — reinforcing the original caution against reading dev_k at face value.

Per-config means (pooled across K/slice) stayed in the same relative order as the original table: C3/C5 lowest (dev_mean 0.068/0.087 vs noiseSD_mean 0.110/0.104), C1/C6 closest to their own noise floor (0.117/0.125, 0.120/0.138) — no config changed which side of the noise floor it sits on.

Decision: TOL=0.15 kept, not re-tuned. The margin between TOL and the noise median widened (old ratio ≈1.04×, new ≈1.25×) purely because the noise floor fell while TOL stayed fixed. Raising toward the new p90 (≈0.17) was considered and rejected as 'chasing noise'; the term this threshold gates is also currently inert in production (lambda_domain_balance frozen at 0.0, not in Optuna's search space, §4.18/§22), so there is no live training consequence. Would revisit if a future re-measurement showed the noise median climbing above 0.15.

Single-fit vs multi-fit reliability: averaging several aligned seeds' r_k readings would give a materially more reliable point estimate (the 'stability/consensus across seeds' idea already named in §10), but the in-loop penalty must compute r_k from the model's current parameters at every training epoch — 'average over 5 seeds' is inherently post-hoc/multi-run and cannot be the in-loop training signal. Multi-seed averaging is available for the outer-loop audit after Optuna picks a config, but a further limit: if seeds land in substantively different, comparably-good local optima (§9's non-convexity), more seeds sharpen the estimate of that uncertainty rather than eliminating it.

Correction to this session's own earlier characterization: not all M_* relations are 'unweighted binary' — verified directly against chunk12.py. The 5 grammar relations (M_Atom_Child, M_Child_Parent, M_Fringe_Cousin, M_Cousin_Parent, M_Cousin_Child) are genuinely unweighted (build_grammar_csr, weight≡1). The 3 anchor relations (M_Parent_Art, M_Child_Art, M_Cousin_Art) carry real tf-idf weighting (build_anchor_csr: weight=log1p(tf)·idf[hyperedge], idf=log(N_articles/doc_freq)+1, chunk12.py:258,315-321) that shapes U_final/U_prob continuously through training, not just at SVD-init. Scope narrow: only 4 of 9 facets (parent_he, core_child_he, cousin_he, art) touch an idf-weighted relation.

Degree-concentration table, row max÷mean (T1/T2): S_Art_Auth (already damped, reference) 7.5×/2.8×; M_Atom_Child 13.0×/16.6×; M_Child_Parent 7.1×/11.2×; M_Fringe_Cousin 6.4×/7.4×; M_Cousin_Parent 7.9×/5.1×; M_Cousin_Child 5.3×/5.2×(row), 5.3×/12.2×(col); S_Art_Journ 1.0×/1.0×(row, trivial), 5.8×/6.5×(col).

All 5 grammar relations show degree concentration comparable to or worse than S_Art_Auth's already-damped case; M_Atom_Child is the worst in the entire topology and currently receives no damping. Connects directly to §9's already-documented limitation that ubiquitous semantic elements are structurally disfavoured. Extending weighting to these relations is a concrete, evidence-backed candidate fix.

What S_Art_Auth's log-damping actually does, verified exactly: damped_mass=log2(1+degree); weight(r,c)=count(r,c)*damped_mass/degree. Confirmed to match the real matrix to 4 decimal places (article 17, degree=65, actual_mass=6.0444=predicted log2(66)=6.0444).

Two effects behave oppositely: total row mass for degree 65 vs degree 6 has raw ratio 10.8×, post-damping mass ratio 2.15× (still monotonically more, but compressed). Per-tie weight reverses rather than compresses: degree-65 article's per-tie weight is 0.093, degree-6 article's is 0.468 — each tie in the smaller article counts 5× more individually.

The per-tie redistribution — not just total-mass compression — is the actual mechanism serving the stated design goal (avoiding mono-article communities built around one high-author-count article): without it a 65-author mega-collaboration could pull all 65 co-authors strongly toward one community; any extension to grammar relations should preserve this per-tie property deliberately, not just replicate total-mass compression.

Recommendation as originally written (superseded by execution, kept for history): extend the anchor idf formula to S_Art_Journ (low risk, no new mechanism); extend S_Art_Auth-style degree log-damping to the 5 grammar relations, M_Atom_Child first. Real cost noted: chunk12.py is the data-generation layer underneath this session's cached fits — changing it invalidates that cache, a substantially larger blast radius than any chunk13v9.py-level change made this session.
